st: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your fingers.
Pound or mash the shallots, garlic, chilies and [[0.5 tsp]] shrimp paste into a rough paste.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Fry the paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the rice and stir-fry for 4 minutes, pressing to break it up.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] kecap manis, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] white pepper until evenly brown.
Push the rice aside, add [[1 tbsp]] oil and fry 2 of the 3 eggs, scrambling them and mixing in.
Divide the fried rice between two plates.
Fry the last egg sunny side up in a little oil until the white is fully set and place on top, with cucumber slices.
Blend the shallots, garlic, galangal, ginger, soaked and drained chilies and [[1 tsp]] turmeric into a smooth paste with a splash of the coconut milk.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste for 6 minutes until fragrant.
Add the beef, lemongrass and lime leaves and stir 5 minutes to coat.
Pour in the [[2 can]] of coconut milk, [[1 tbsp]] tamarind, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[2 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a gentle boil, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 2.5 hours, stirring every 15 minutes.
When the sauce thickens and turns oily, stir constantly for 15 minutes more until the beef is dark brown and almost dry.
Taste for salt, remove lemongrass and lime leaves, and serve with rice.
Mix the chicken with [[2 tbsp]] kecap manis, [[2 clove]] garlic, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, [[1 tsp]] coriander and [[1 tbsp]] oil. Marinate 30 minutes.
For the sauce, grind [[0.75 cup]] peanuts, the chilies, shallots and [[2 clove]] garlic into a coarse paste.
Fry the paste in [[1 tbsp]] oil for 3 minutes, then add [[0.5 cup]] water, [[1 tbsp]] kecap manis, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Simmer 8 minutes until thick, then stir in [[1 tbsp]] lime juice.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers.
Grill or broil on high, turning, for 10 minutes until charred at the edges and 165°F (74°C) inside.
Serve with the peanut sauce.
Boil the potatoes whole for 20 minutes, then peel and slice. Boil the eggs in a separate pot for 10 minutes, cool and peel.
Blanch the green beans 3 minutes, cabbage 1 minute, and sprouts 30 seconds. Cool in cold water.
Fry the tofu and tempeh in [[0.25 cup]] oil for 3 minutes per side until golden. Drain.
Grind [[0.75 cup]] peanuts with the garlic, chilies and [[1 tsp]] salt to a paste.
Whisk in [[2 tbsp]] kecap manis, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, [[1 tbsp]] lime juice and [[0.5 cup]] warm water to make a pourable sauce.
Arrange the vegetables, potatoes, tofu, tempeh and halved eggs on a platter.
Pour the sauce over and serve right away.
Put the chicken, [[8 cup]] water, lemongrass, lime leaves and [[2 tsp]] salt in a pot. Boil, skimming foam.
Simmer 35 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C). Remove the chicken, shred the meat and strain the broth.
Blend the garlic, ginger, shallots and [[1 tbsp]] turmeric with a splash of broth into a paste.
Fry the paste in [[2 tbsp]] oil for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Stir the paste into the broth with [[0.5 tsp]] white pepper and simmer 10 minutes.
Divide noodles and sprouts among bowls and top with shredded chicken and halved eggs.
Ladle on the hot broth and add [[0.25 cup]] fried shallots with lime wedges.
Pulse the beef, [[2 clove]] garlic, shallots, [[2 tsp]] salt, [[1 tsp]] white pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] baking powder in a food processor until a sticky paste.
Add [[0.5 cup]] tapioca starch and [[0.25 cup]] ice water and pulse until smooth.
Bring a pot of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into 1.5 inch balls and drop into the water.
Simmer 10 minutes until they float and reach 160°F (71°C). Remove.
Heat [[8 cup]] beef broth with [[2 clove]] garlic fried briefly in oil. Boil the noodles in water for 4 minutes, and blanch the bok choy 1 minute.
Fill bowls with noodles, bok choy and meatballs and ladle over the hot broth. Top with [[0.25 cup]] fried shallots.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until just tender, about 4 minutes. Drain, rinse and toss with a drizzle of oil.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wok over high heat and cook the shallots and garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 4 minutes until fully cooked through at 165°F (74°C).
Push to one side, add [[1 tbsp]] oil and scramble the 2 eggs.
Add the cabbage and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add the noodles with [[3 tbsp]] kecap manis, [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce and [[0.25 tsp]] white pepper and toss for 3 minutes.
Top with scallions and serve hot.

ing: stemmed, such as Fresno or Thai
st: Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and fry the chilies, shallots, garlic and tomato for 6 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Add [[1 tsp]] shrimp paste and mash it with the back of a spoon for 1 minute.
Move everything to a mortar or small food processor.
Grind coarsely, adding [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] sugar.
Return to the pan with [[2 tbsp]] oil and cook 4 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] lime juice, taste, and adjust.
Cool and keep in a jar in the fridge for up to 1 week.
Whisk [[2 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] yeast, [[3 tbsp]] sugar, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and 2 eggs with [[1.25 cup]] warm milk into a smooth batter.
Rest, covered, for 1 hour until bubbly.
Stir in [[0.5 tsp]] baking soda just before cooking.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and pour in a thick layer of batter.
Cover and cook 5 minutes without flipping until the top is full of holes and set.
Brush with [[2 tbsp]] butter and sprinkle on the chocolate, peanuts, cheese and [[3 tbsp]] condensed milk.
Fold in half, brush with [[2 tbsp]] butter, cut and serve hot.
Mash the garlic with [[1 tsp]] coriander, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Stir in [[0.25 cup]] water to make a marinade.
Coat the tempeh slices and let sit for 15 minutes.
Heat [[0.75 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the tempeh 3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain the tempeh on paper towels.
Serve warm with sambal and rice.
Blend the pandan leaves with [[1 cup]] water and strain to get green liquid.
Whisk [[0.5 cup]] rice flour and [[2 tbsp]] tapioca starch with the pandan water and [[1 cup]] more water in a pot.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 6 minutes until thick and glossy.
Press through a colander with large holes into a bowl of ice water to form short jelly strands.
Simmer [[0.5 cup]] palm sugar with [[0.5 cup]] water for 8 minutes into a syrup.
Warm [[1.5 cup]] coconut milk with [[0.25 tsp]] salt, then cool.
Divide the strands among glasses, add [[3 cup]] crushed ice, coconut milk and palm sugar syrup.
Mix the rice flour, pandan extract and warm water in a bowl. Knead 3 minutes into a smooth, soft dough that does not stick to your hands. Add a little water if dry.
Pinch off pieces the size of a large grape and flatten each into a small disc in your palm.
Put about 1 teaspoon of palm sugar in the center, fold the dough around it, and roll into a smooth ball, sealing well so the sugar cannot leak.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Drop in the balls in batches. They are done 2 to 3 minutes after they float.
Steam the grated coconut with the salt and [[1 tbsp]] sugar for 10 minutes if using fresh, then cool.
Lift the balls out with a slotted spoon, drain well, and roll in the coconut. Serve warm or at room temperature.
nt: Boiled, then rolled in steamed coconut
Best swap: dark brown sugar, chopped into small bits, instead of palm sugar, same amount.

st: Mix the chicken, carrot, scallions, garlic, kecap manis, white pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until well combined and sticky.
Put a teaspoon of filling in the center of each wrapper. Brush the edges with egg white, fold into a triangle and press out the air.
Brush one corner with egg white, then bring the two bottom corners together and press them to make a little pouch.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F. Test it: a wrapper scrap should bubble and float right away.
Fry 5 or 6 dumplings at a time for 3 minutes, turning once, until deep golden. The chicken must reach 165°F.
Drain on a rack or paper towels and serve hot with the sweet chili sauce.
nt: Deep fried
Best swap: air fry at 380°F for 8 minutes, spraying with oil, for less oil. Use ground pork or shrimp in place of chicken.

st: Warm the sugar with the water in a small pot just until dissolved, about 2 minutes, then cool.
Mix the coconut milk, condensed milk and cooled syrup in a pitcher and chill for 20 minutes.
Divide the coconut meat, avocado cubes and sliced jackfruit among four tall glasses.
Pour the sweet coconut milk over the fruit, filling each glass about two thirds.
Top with crushed ice and stir gently.
Serve immediately with a long spoon so the ice stays icy.
nt: Don't cook: assembled and chilled
Best swap: use canned jackfruit in syrup, drained, if fresh is unavailable, or use evaporated milk instead of coconut milk.

st: Blend the shallots, garlic, chilies, turmeric and [[1 tsp]] salt with [[2 tbsp]] oil into a smooth paste. Fry it in a pan over medium heat for 6 minutes until aromatic.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] tamarind paste and [[3 tbsp]] kecap manis and cook 2 minutes until thick. Cool slightly.
Slash the fish 3 times per side. Rub with [[2 tbsp]] lime juice and rest 10 minutes, then rub the spice paste all over and inside.
Marinate the fish in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Heat a grill to medium-high, about 425°F, and oil the grate. Grill the fish 6 to 7 minutes per side, basting with leftover paste, until it flakes and reads 140°F.
Serve hot with steamed rice, sliced cucumber and sambal.
nt: Grilled over medium-high charcoal heat, basted with sweet soy
Best swap: bake wrapped in banana leaf or foil at 400°F for 25 minutes. Use brown sugar plus soy (1 tbsp : 3 tbsp) for kecap manis.

st: Heat the frying oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Fry the tempeh matchsticks in batches until crisp and golden, about 3 minutes each. Drain on paper towels.
Pour off all but [[2 tbsp]] of the oil. Fry the shallots, garlic, chilies, galangal and bay leaves over medium heat for 3 minutes until fragrant and softened.
Add [[3 tbsp]] kecap manis, [[1 tbsp]] palm sugar and [[2 tbsp]] water. Stir until the sugar melts and the sauce bubbles, about 1 minute.
Return the tempeh to the wok and toss for 2 minutes until each piece is lacquered and the sauce is nearly gone.
Taste and add salt if needed. Serve with rice.
nt: Deep fried, then stir fried
Best swap: for kecap manis use 2 tbsp soy sauce plus 1 tbsp brown sugar; or oven-bake the tempeh at 400°F for 20 minutes.

st: Halve 2 ripe avocados, remove the pits, and scoop the flesh into a blender.
Add [[3 tbsp]] condensed milk and [[1 cup]] cold milk.
Blend for 45 seconds until silky smooth with no lumps, then add [[1 cup]] ice and pulse 10 seconds.
Swirl [[1 tbsp]] chocolate syrup on the inside of each tall glass, using a spoon, and add [[1 tbsp]] condensed milk to the bottom if you like it sweet.
Pour the avocado mixture in, drizzle [[1 tbsp]] more chocolate syrup on top, and serve at once with a long spoon.
nt: Don't cook: just blend
Best swap: use coconut milk and palm sugar syrup in place of dairy and condensed milk for a dairy-free version.

ing: egg roll or spring roll wrappers
st: Cook the beef in a skillet over medium-high heat with the shallot and garlic until no pink remains, about 6 minutes. Add the curry powder, pepper and salt, then cool slightly.
Beat the eggs in a bowl and mix in the cooled beef and the scallions.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Lay one wrapper in the pan and pour a quarter of the egg filling onto its center.
Fold the four corners of the wrapper in over the filling to make a neat square parcel, pressing the edges down.
Cook about 3 minutes until golden, flip, and cook another 3 minutes until the egg inside is fully set and firm to the touch. Keep warm and repeat.
Cut into squares and serve hot with the pickled cucumber and a spoonful of chili sauce.
nt: Pan-fried parcels in shallow oil
Best swap: use ground chicken or crumbled firm tofu 1 to 1 for the beef; flour tortillas can stand in for the wrappers.

st: Put the rice, chicken, water, ginger, garlic, turmeric and salt in a heavy pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer with the lid slightly open.
Cook for 40 minutes, stirring from the bottom every 10 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the rice breaks down.
Lift out the chicken and shred the meat, discarding the bones and skin. Make sure it reaches 165°F and no pink remains.
Continue simmering the porridge for 20 more minutes, stirring often, until it is thick, creamy and spoon-coating. Add water to loosen.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool in cold water and peel. Halve them.
Ladle the porridge into bowls. Top with shredded chicken, an egg, fried shallots, celery leaves and crullers, then drizzle with soy sauce.
nt: Simmered low and slow
Best swap: use leftover cooked rice, 2 cups, simmered with the broth for 25 minutes when you need a shortcut.

ing: fresh, with water and soft flesh
st: Hack off the top of each young coconut with a heavy knife, or cut a small hole, and pour the coconut water into a pitcher. You should get about [[1.5 cup]] in total.
Strain the water through a fine sieve to catch any shell bits.
Scoop out the soft white flesh with a spoon and slice it into thin strips.
Divide the flesh between two tall glasses and add [[1 cup]] of crushed ice between them.
Stir [[3 tbsp]] palm sugar syrup and a pinch of salt into the coconut water, then pour it over the ice.
Squeeze in a wedge of lime and stir. Serve right away with a long spoon to eat the flesh.
nt: Don't cook: just open, scoop and chill
Best swap: [[1.5 cup]] store-bought coconut water and a 14 oz can of young coconut meat if fresh nuts are unavailable.

st: Blend the shallots, garlic and chilies with [[2 tbsp]] water to a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Fry the paste with the curry powder for 4 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the beef and cook 3 minutes, then the shrimp and tomatoes and cook 2 minutes until the shrimp turn pink.
Pour in the stock and kecap manis and simmer for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile boil the noodles for 2 minutes in water, then drain well.
Add the noodles and bean sprouts to the wok and toss for 2 minutes until the sauce coats the noodles and the sprouts barely soften. Serve with lime wedges.
nt: Stir fried, finished in a spiced sauce
Best swap: replace the Aceh curry powder with 1 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp cumin and 1 tsp coriander; use chicken or tofu for beef.
